inputs.share_count_basis: 7,303.739m shares issued less 187.387m treasury shares held for the restricted share award schemes = 7,116.352m at 2026-06-30 (interim note 20/23b). No share options outstanding (all 2025 options exercised or lapsed); FY2025 note 13 states diluted EPS = basic. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so vesting of the treasury shares is already charged.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents 1,517.312 + short-term bank deposits 84.834 at 2026-06-30. Net debt = bank borrowings 2,316.349 - 1,602.146 = 714.2, matching the company's own gearing definition (interim MD&A). Lease liabilities (79.083) are EXCLUDED under lease treatment (B). Borrowings are 99.9% short-term at June-30; post-period the bank extended US$799.7m to March 2029 (interim Subsequent Events).
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income FY2025 was US$23.719m but is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt (US$714m), not net-cash, and the component build is unlevered (both finance income and the US$78.5m interest paid sit outside EBIT), so the cash pile is counted once, in the net-debt bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash-flow statement, 'Share-based payments expense (Note 30)' US$9,491k (6088.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:6837). No separate equity-award tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow 'Shares purchased for share award scheme' US$2.48m; nil in H1 FY2026. No open-market buyback programme; the flat count is a modelling convention funded by SBC expense, not by repurchases.
inputs.fx_note: USD/HKD 7.8428 from Yahoo Finance HKD=X on 2026-10-23 (HKD pegged 7.75-7.85 band, so the rate is stable). Statements, flows and WACC are in USD; the HKEX quote is HKD. Per-share values computed in USD then multiplied by 7.8428. No dual listing exists for a parity check; the peg itself bounds the error at ~0.6%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the flows' currency: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta 1.45 (HK-listed, China/Vietnam/India/Mexico manufacturing footprint, 31% single-customer cluster) = cost of equity ~11.5%; pre-tax cost of debt 3.68% (weighted average on unsecured bank borrowings at 2026-06-30, interim note 21) = ~2.6% after 30% tax; target D/V 30% (current gross-debt/EV ~40% is inflated by short-term working-capital borrowings). 0.7 x 11.5 + 0.3 x 2.6 = 8.8%, rounded to 9.0%. One WACC across all scenarios: cyclicality, customer concentration and the AI-cloud dependence are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. The full lease payment (FY2025 principal US$17.7m + lease interest ~US$3m = ~0.4% of revenue) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (US$79.1m) are excluded from net debt; da_pct is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 281.3 - ~19 ROU = ~262 = 5.2% of revenue; H1 FY2026 ROU depreciation 9.0m of 134.8m total).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (US$15.5m stock at 2026-06-30, <US$1m of profit). Flows are consolidated; the NCI stock is deducted once in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (FY2026-FY2035) because capex is still normalising from the FY2024-25 footprint build-out and the margin path is not flat until year 3-5. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating industrial manufacturer (connectors, cables, harnesses, acoustics) -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (USD filer / HKD quote, IFRS-16 leases, NCI, cyclical, near-SBC-zero). Business: Foxconn (Hon Hai) controlled interconnect maker; FY2025 revenue US$5,003m across smartphones 16%, cloud/AI server 16% (+38% FY25, +56% H1 FY26), consumer interconnects 17%, auto mobility 19% (Auto-Kabel acquired Dec-2024, now 'One Mobility'), system products/acoustics 27%. Customer A (a brand company and its nominated contract manufacturers, i.e. the Apple supply chain) was 31% of H1 FY2026 revenue; Customer B (Hon Hai group) 11%. FY0 anchors: EBITDA 568.2 (11.4%), D&A 281.3, capex 420.4 (8.4%), cash tax 106.8 (37% of EBIT, inflated by PRC withholding tax on dividends and prior-year settlements; H1 FY2026 P&L rate 27%), owner FCF -162.8 (third consecutive negative year: FY2023 +300, FY2024 -132, FY2025 -162). H1 FY2026: revenue +8.3%, gross margin 19.1% (+0.5pp), operating margin 3.0% (vs 4.6%, FX), OCF 33.7, capex 199 (vs 284). Working capital is modelled NEGATIVE on growth: inventories 1,098 + trade receivables 923 - trade payables 698 = NWC ~US$1.32bn, ~26% of revenue, so each dollar of growth consumes ~18-20c of cash. The qualitative Analysis.json was not present at build time; the business read is from the FY2025 annual and H1 FY2026 interim directly. No current-FY numeric guidance is given; management says cloud/data-center 'sustains strong growth' in 2026, consumer interconnects hit by memory shortages, auto mobility down on US EV contraction.

equity_bridge.note: Interim balance sheet 2026-06-30 (USD'000 15,526); deducted once, flows are consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: equity 3yr CAGR 4.6% and revenue 3yr CAGR 3.4%, lifted to 5% for the AI-cloud mix shift; this is the average of the base-case 10-year growth path
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR of 29.7% diverges >30% from equity 5yr CAGR 4.2% because the FY2020 base year (EPS US$0.006, COVID trough) is depressed; EPS 3yr CAGR is -2.9%. Equity CAGR is the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped because the company is net-debt): FY2020 -259.7, FY2021 -158.9, FY2022 +422.9, FY2023 +300.0, FY2024 -132.1, FY2025 -162.8. CAGRs are undefined on a series that is negative at both ends; cumulative FY2023-25 owner FCF is +US$5m on US$1.08bn of capex, i.e. the last three years of growth have been funded by borrowings (bank debt 1,027 -> 2,316 from FY2022 to H1 FY2026). Reported FCF CAGR is equally undefined; SBC is <0.2% of revenue so SBC is not the cause.

base.growth_rationale: H1 FY2026 +8.3% with cloud +56% offsetting consumer -21% and auto -6%; FY2026 and FY2027 held at 8% as cloud (now 22% of revenue) keeps compounding and the memory-shortage drag on consumer interconnects fades, then decays to 2.5% as AI-server copper interconnect growth normalises and the Apple-cluster smartphone/acoustics book stays flat.
base.margin_rationale: Post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin 8.5-12.9% over FY2018-25 (FY2025 11.4%; H1 FY2026 ~8.6% on FX and seasonality). 10.5% for FY2026 reflecting the weak H1, recovering to the 11.5% decade mid-point as cloud mix rises and Auto-Kabel integration costs roll off. No credit for a structural step-up above the historical range.
base.capex_rationale: Capex 8.6%/8.4% of revenue in FY2024/25 for the Vietnam/India/Mexico/Europe footprint; H1 FY2026 at ~8% but down 30% YoY. Glides to 5.5%, roughly D&A ex-ROU (5.2-5.3%), from FY2032.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 37% of EBIT in FY2025 (PRC dividend withholding + prior-year settlements), P&L rate 34% FY2025 and 27% H1 FY2026 (no withholding, transfer-pricing optimisation). 32% ramping to a 30% blended cash rate across PRC 25%, Taiwan 20%, Germany ~30%, US 21%, Vietnam/India incentives, plus recurring withholding on upstreaming.

scenario_narratives.base: The AI-server copper interconnect book (cabinet connectors and cable modules, 22% of H1 FY2026 revenue, +56%) keeps compounding for two more years and then normalises, while the Apple-cluster smartphone and EarPods business and the Hon Hai-related system products stay a flat, low-margin volume base. Consumer interconnects recover from the FY2026 memory shortage; auto mobility (Auto-Kabel/One Mobility) stays subdued on US EV contraction. EBITDA margin recovers from the FX-hit H1 FY2026 to the 11.5% decade mid-point, the FY2024-25 footprint capex rolls off to maintenance levels by FY2032, and ~18c of every dollar of growth is absorbed by inventory and receivables. Owner FCF is roughly break-even in FY2026, positive from FY2027 and ~3% of revenue at maturity; the valuation rests heavily on the terminal year because the explicit years are capex- and working-capital-heavy.
scenario_narratives.bull: FIT becomes a tier-one supplier to the global AI-server platforms (NVIDIA/hyperscaler cabinet connectors, high-speed cable modules, optical co-packaging) and cloud grows to a third of revenue by FY2028 at structurally higher margins, lifting group EBITDA margin to 13.5%, above anything in the decade's history. One Mobility wins European/USMCA high-voltage harness and busbar programmes as EV penetration resumes, the memory-constrained consumer book normalises in FY2027, working capital turns improve with mix, and capex falls to maintenance by FY2031. Tax normalises to 28% as transfer-pricing optimisation holds. This path requires several independent things to go right: AI-server share, auto programme wins and margin discipline simultaneously.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI-server interconnect demand is cyclical rather than secular: hyperscaler capex digests in FY2027-28, copper-based cabinet products are commoditised by Taiwanese/Chinese competitors (and by optical substitution), and growth collapses to 2% after a 4% FY2026. The Apple cluster (31% of revenue) continues to move share to alternative suppliers and to India-based assembly where FIT is subscale, system products remain hostage to supply-chain and spec changes, and auto mobility stays loss-making on US EV weakness and German restructuring. EBITDA margin settles at 10%, FX (TWD/RMB strength) and PRC withholding keep cash tax at 32%, and the terminal multiple is capped at 12x. The US$2.3bn of bank debt, 99.9% short-term at June-30 (US$800m since extended to 2029), keeps refinancing risk live if cash flow does not turn.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: three consecutive years of negative owner FCF funded by short-term bank debt, a 31% single-customer cluster, Hon Hai control (related-party sales and governance), and the stock's 52-week range (3.49-10.89) showing the AI-interconnect narrative has already partly unwound. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs AI-server share, auto programme wins and a margin level above the decade's historical ceiling to coincide. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A Foxconn-controlled interconnect manufacturer valued as a low-margin, capex- and working-capital-intensive cyclical with one genuinely growing segment (AI-server copper interconnect). The house view gives the cloud segment two more years of strong growth and a margin recovery to the decade's mid-point, but no structural re-rating above the historical margin range and no credit for the multiple the market paid at the 52-week high. Value is terminal-heavy because the explicit years carry footprint capex and working-capital absorption; the question for an owner is whether FY2027+ owner FCF actually turns positive, which it has not been since FY2023.
key_risks_to_valuation: Customer concentration: Customer A (Apple cluster) 31% and Customer B (Hon Hai group) 11% of H1 FY2026 revenue; a share loss or spec change moves the whole smartphone/acoustics book
AI-server interconnect cyclicality and commoditisation: the only segment growing above GDP; hyperscaler capex digestion or optical substitution removes the growth leg

Cash conversion: owner FCF negative FY2024-25 and only break-even in base FY2026; NWC ~26% of revenue so growth consumes cash, and US$2.3bn of borrowings were 99.9% short-term at June-30 (US$800m extended to 2029 post-period)
FX: USD reporting with TWD/RMB/EUR cost bases; H1 FY2026 operating margin fell 1.6pp 'primarily due to exchange rates'
Governance: Hon Hai controls the register and is a top-two customer and related-party supplier; minority holders have no say on capital allocation (no dividend since FY2019)
Tax: PRC withholding on upstreamed profits and transfer-pricing changes swing the cash tax rate between 27% and 37%
Terminal-value dependence: ~65-70% of base EV sits in the terminal; a 1pp WACC move is worth ~15-20% of value

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 3.49-10.89. FX USD/HKD from Yahoo HKD=X same day.
